scope: Bounded owner repair and native publication ID migration inventory; audit snapshot only, not a replacement runtime property schema.

fixed.authority: Existing HostState a11y_owner marker, observed weakly by A11yOwner in shared A11yProvenance
fixed.change: Accessibility::sync and publication_requests/bind_publication require owner. Native/browser freeze it at publication. Queue preserves existing bindings and removes its separate owner-identity field. Foreign requests cannot acquire new owner at re-enqueue.
fixed.compatibility: Implementers and bind_publication/publication_requests callers must pass the host owner. All four workspace Accessibility implementations migrated. Raw constructors still name the current live context.

fixed.change: Direct bound/raw requests now return Cancelled after take_disposal even while runner/layout remain inspectable. Disposed host stops invoking Accessibility::sync.
attach returns Result; a different Arc window handle is refused before changing the stored window, while the same handle is idempotent. Native host creation propagates failure.
fixed.verification: Headless handle-admission regression using the exact attachment helper. No claim of headed platform installation or recovery.

native_id_migration.status: Open; intentionally exceeds this bounded repair. Owner-bound requests do not make reused raw OS numeric IDs safe.
native_id_migration.cause: Native map_parts resolves TreeId/NodeId through last published requests. An old OS event arriving after replacement can still select a new binding. Shared published request binding contains no OS originating generation.
native_id_migration.full_node_identity_gap: SemanticProjection publication_requests covers DOM targets and producer action buttons. Producer structural children are separate generated tree nodes without routing entries; an action-map-only allocator does not cover all published node identities.
native_id_migration.guest_boundary: Node.tree_id and TreeUpdate.tree_id are tree identities; never rewrite host/guest node IDs through an unqualified shared numeric map. Current Cambium A11yHost routes only ROOT; embedded batch routing is separate.
native_id_migration.ingress: A11yActionRequest preserves action/tree/node/data, not originating publication life. Bridge activation epochs govern activation/replay, not target lifetime.
done_conditions: Shared projection provides owner/contributor/child identity for every published node, including structural and non-action nodes.
One native publication namespace assigns nonreused IDs per authored life; ordinary frames preserve IDs and unaffected focus.
Rewrite all typed references using an authoritative schema-owned remapper; receive all eight vectors, seven scalar relations, both text selection positions, root and focus.
Preserve TreeId ownership through root/guest install and ingress, including selection references if selection routing is added.
Actual old/late native event after replacement refuses; normal value updates preserve identity; install/reset/reattach and guest cases have headed receipts.
rejected_shortcuts: Deriving complete publication identity from action route maps alone
Treating bridge activation epochs as target-life generations
Fresh ID for every frame or a second maintained Node property schema in Mere

remaining_ownership_migrations: Adapter-to-host/window/canvas handoff remains separately governed. A11yHost now refuses replacing its attached handle, but this does not qualify physical installation, partial failure/reset recovery, or moving an adapter to another host with the same surface.
Custom hosts must keep marker alive while live, dispose it once, and create a fresh marker for a new lifetime; reviving a disposed marker violates the contract.
Generic producer actor activation is not atomic with semantic observation; optional child tokens still rely on legacy nonreuse.
Canvas raw callback same-UUID remove/recreate visibility.
Rootstock intrinsic sizing and Path-B scene raster wiring.
Actual browser proxy/focus/disposal, native install/late-event/reattach behavior and human AT remain unqualified.
